elements.element: The licence extends to Customer's affiliates.
elements.evidence: Added sentence: "The license granted in Section 4(c) extends to Company's affiliates upon written notice to Contractor". "Company" is defined as Clear Capital alone, so this is the only affiliate coverage and it is not duplicative.

elements.element: The licence extends to contractors acting on Customer's behalf.
elements.evidence: Neither Section 4(c) nor the inserted sentence names contractors acting on Company's behalf; the sublicence right is a separate mechanic and does not expressly extend the grant to Company's contractors. Fix: add "and to contractors acting on Company's behalf" to the grant.
Section 4(c) grants a "royalty-free, non-exclusive perpetual license" — the paid-up/royalty-free grant is expressly perpetual.
Section 4(c) says "perpetual" but contains no "irrevocable" qualifier, and none was added. Fix: insert "irrevocable" into the Section 4(c) grant.

elements.element: A subscription licence is terminable only for uncured material breach.
elements.evidence: Conditional element: the agreement contains no subscription licence — the only grant is a perpetual royalty-free licence in Contractor's Information under an MSA — so the condition does not apply.

elements.element: The licence is transferable to Customer's successors.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "Company may transfer that license, without Contractor's approval, to a successor in a merger or acquisition transaction." Note the transfer right is limited to M&A successors rather than successors generally, which is the fallback formulation rather than the full preferred breadth.

elements.element: Customer's affiliates are covered on written notice.
elements.evidence: "...extends to Company's affiliates upon written notice to Contractor" — express affiliate extension conditioned on written notice, exactly the fallback mechanic. Affiliate use through an affiliate's authorised personnel follows from the grant; no separate personnel edit needed.

elements.element: The licence is transferable to a successor in a merger or acquisition transaction.
elements.evidence: "Company may transfer that license, without Contractor's approval, to a successor in a merger or acquisition transaction" — a direct without-approval permission, not a broad notwithstanding override of Section 10.

reasons: Fallback level is complete: both fallback elements are met in operative language by a single appended sentence to Section 4(c) (affiliates on written notice; transfer to an M&A successor without Contractor approval). The claimed deviation status and fallback target are correct, since the original Section 4(c) ran only to Clear Capital and Section 10 barred transfer without consent.

Preferred level is incomplete for two reasons the drafter would need to repair if pursuing it: (i) no express extension to "contractors acting on Company's behalf" in the grant, and (ii) no express "irrevocable" qualifier on the perpetual paid-up grant. The successor-transfer wording is also limited to merger/acquisition successors rather than successors generally.

Minimal: the edit is one concise insertion, adds no survival tail, expense, procedure, or notice-period boilerplate, and does not touch the favourable existing perpetual/royalty-free/sublicensable grant or delete any word (including the Customer-favourable "non-exclusive" and consent-not-unreasonably-withheld language in Section 10). No duplicate affiliate coverage arises because "Company" is defined as Clear Capital alone with no affiliate inclusion.

Preserves intent: Section 10's general non-assignment of the Agreement survives and continues to govern assignment of the Agreement and obligations; the inserted sentence is a specific, self-executing permission limited to the Section 4(c) licence, avoiding a broad "notwithstanding" override, and leaves no undefined term or dangling cross-reference (Section 4(c) is cited accurately).

Drafting nit only (not a defect): "affiliates" is used without a defined term in the Agreement; if the counterparty pushes back, add a short definition of Affiliate (control-based) rather than expanding the operative grant.
